about: fl-headless teaching mode: plain-language notes per tool and concept. beginner = no jargon, pro = terse. Extend freely.

fl_review.beginner: Listened to the song section by section and measured how loud, how wide and how bright each part is.
fl_review.pro: Per-section LUFS / correlation / band balance with a ranked issue list.
fl_review.why: A song feels right when the big moments are louder than the quiet ones and nothing sounds muddy or harsh - this checks that with numbers so your ears can focus on the music.
fl_review.next: Pick the top issue and fix it, then review again to see it gone.

fl_doctor.beginner: Looked through the project file for problems: missing samples, plugins you may not own, unused channels, notes that clash.
fl_doctor.pro: Static .flp lint: ownership, missing samples, routing, automation targets, clashes.
fl_doctor.why: Catching these early saves a nasty surprise when you render or share the project.

fl_mix_engineer.beginner: Listened to the mix and suggested level, pan and EQ moves (it only changes things if you said apply).
fl_mix_engineer.pro: Measured mix proposal (faders / pans / EQ / comp moves); apply=true writes them, revert_last undoes.
fl_mix_engineer.why: A second pair of ears on balance: what's buried, what's too loud, what fights for the same space.
fl_mix_engineer.next: Listen, then apply the moves you agree with.

fl_finalize.beginner: Rendered the song and made the finished master file at the loudness your collection uses.
fl_finalize.pro: Render + true-peak limit + finish to the profile target, filed as the final.
fl_finalize.why: Every song in a collection should end up at a matching loudness so they play well side by side.
fl_finalize.next: Listen to the final on headphones and on a phone speaker.

fl_render.beginner: Had FL export the song to an audio file.
fl_render.why: An audio file is what you listen to, measure and share.

fl_render_stems.beginner: Exported each instrument as its own audio file (a 'stem').
fl_render_stems.why: Stems let someone else mix or remix the song without needing your plugins.

fl_listen.beginner: Recorded what FL played so it could be measured.
fl_listen.why: Measuring the real sound beats guessing from settings.

flh_sync.beginner: Sent all the waiting edits to FL in one go.
flh_sync.pro: Applied lazy-queued edits in one save + reload.
flh_sync.why: Big projects take long to reload, so edits are collected and sent together.

flp_edit.beginner: Changed the project file directly (a backup was kept).
flp_edit.why: Several changes at once means FL only has to reload once.

flp_edit_notes.beginner: Changed notes in a pattern (moved, transposed, tightened or loosened them).
flp_edit_notes.pro: Note ops on a channel/pattern range.
flp_edit_notes.why: Small note fixes often matter more than any plugin.

flp_perform.beginner: Made the playing feel more human: tiny timing and loudness changes, like a real player.
flp_perform.pro: Applied the performance spec (tempo map, dynamics, humanize).
flp_perform.why: Perfectly even notes sound robotic; small variations make music breathe.
flp_perform.next: Listen; flp_perform_undo goes back if it's too much.

flp_perform_setup.beginner: Worked out which parts are which and prepared a 'performance' plan for them.
flp_perform_setup.pro: Built the performance spec from the project.

flp_remove_channels.beginner: Removed (or, in a dry run, listed) channels from the project.
flp_remove_channels.why: Unused channels make a project harder to read and slower to load.

flp_collect_samples.beginner: Copied every sample the project uses into one folder next to it.
flp_collect_samples.why: Then the project still opens on another PC or after you move folders.

flp_export_midi.beginner: Saved the notes as a MIDI file any music program can open.
flp_export_midi.pro: Type-1 MIDI export with tempo map.

flh_journal.beginner: Read or updated the song's notebook (sections, what you liked, versions).
flh_journal.why: So the next session remembers what this one learned.

flh_profile.beginner: Read or updated your house rules (loudness, plugins you own, colors).

flh_collab_pack.beginner: Put together everything a collaborator needs in one folder: project, samples, MIDI, stems and a readme.
flh_collab_pack.pro: Collab pack (project + samples, MIDI, stems, README, journal summary, zip).
flh_collab_pack.why: Your collaborator can start right away, even without your plugins.
flh_collab_pack.next: Open the copy once yourself to check it loads, then send the zip.

flh_recipe_run.beginner: Ran a saved workflow - several steps in one go.

fl_vocal_setup.beginner: Got a mixer track ready to record your voice (named, colored, armed).
fl_vocal_setup.next: Do the level check before recording.

fl_vocal_level_check.beginner: Listened to your mic while you sang to check the level isn't too quiet or clipping.
fl_vocal_level_check.pro: Input peak/RMS check on the armed insert.
fl_vocal_level_check.why: A good recording level is the one thing you can't fix later.
fl_vocal_level_check.next: Aim for loud parts peaking around -10 to -6 dBFS.

fl_job.beginner: Checked on a task running in the background.

flh_resume.beginner: Summed up where this song stands.

flp_.beginner: Worked on the project file itself (FL doesn't need to be open).

lufs.beginner: LUFS is how loud a song feels overall, as one number. Streaming services turn loud songs down to about -14, so being much louder doesn't help.
lufs.pro: Integrated loudness (ITU-R BS.1770, gated). Platforms normalise around -14 LUFS.

true peak.beginner: The highest point the sound really reaches, including between samples. Keeping it under -1 stops crackle after MP3/streaming conversion.
true peak.pro: Inter-sample peak (4x oversampled); -1 dBTP leaves codec headroom.

stem.beginner: One instrument (or group) exported on its own as audio, lined up from the start of the song.

sidechain.beginner: Making one sound duck out of the way when another plays - like the bass dipping on each kick so both are clear.
sidechain.pro: Gain reduction keyed from another source (here: volume automation via flp_duck).

eq.beginner: Turning frequency ranges up or down - like a fancy bass/treble knob - so instruments don't cover each other.

compression.beginner: Evening out loud and quiet moments of a sound so it sits steadily in the mix.

mud.beginner: A cloudy, boomy sound from too much low-middle (roughly 200-500 Hz) piling up.

harsh.beginner: A tiring, piercing sound from too much upper-middle (roughly 2-5 kHz).

correlation.beginner: How similar left and right speakers are. Near +1 is solid, near 0 is very wide, below 0 can vanish on a phone speaker.
correlation.pro: L/R phase correlation; < 0 risks mono cancellation.

quantize.beginner: Snapping notes onto the beat grid so they line up.

humanize.beginner: Adding tiny random timing and loudness changes so it sounds played, not programmed.

gain staging.beginner: Keeping every track at a healthy level so nothing clips and plugins behave.

mastering.beginner: The final polish that makes a mix ready to release: overall tone, loudness and safe peaks.
